RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the December 4, 2006/Agrahayana 13, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and
Renewable Energy; Power; Science and Technology; Social
Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Women and
Child Development)
Total number of questions — 20
Sachar Committee Report on state of
Muslims
*161. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD:
SHRI PRAVEEN
RASHTRAPAL:
Will the Minister of MINORITY
AFFAIRS  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have examined
the Sachar Committee's report on the state
of Muslims in India;
(b) if so, the salient findings of the Sachar
Committee; and
(c) whether a similar Committee headed
by Dr. Gopal Singh was appointed two
and a half decades ago by Government to
assess the social and economic status of
Muslims and if so, the action taken on its
report by Government?
Sale of Dabhol Power Plant
*162. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have received suggestions for selling of
Dabhol Power Plant;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps Government are taking in
this regard?
Corpus of Maulana Azad
Foundation
*163. MAULANA OBAIDULLAH
KHAN AZMI: Will the Minister of
MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the total corpus of Maulana Azad
Education Foundation as on date;
(b) the details of requests/projects/
applications received for grants during the
last three years and the current year;
(c) the requests/projects/applications in
which grant has been released, alongwith
the amount in each case, year-wise; and
(d) the requests/projects/applications
pending as on date and those not sanctioned
alongwith reasons therefor and the steps
being taken to make the procedure
transparent and web-enabled for online
interaction?

52
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Campuses of foreign education
providers
*164. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have permitted
certain foreign education providers to set
up campuses in the country for imparting
higher education;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the terms and conditions imposed on those
institutions; and
(c) by when these campuses are likely
to start functioning?
Economic development of women
*165. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) the steps taken by her Ministry for
women development in the year 2006-07
to make them economically self-reliant;
(b) whether Gender Budgeting is being
followed by all Ministries; and
(c) if so, the Ministry-wise break-up
thereof?
Achievements on science and
technology
†*166. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of SCIENCE
AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that achievement
and progress in the field of science and
technology of India is not encouraging;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
standard and quality of research-work is
constantly on the decline due to lack of
essential and favourable coordination
between education and research in the
country;
(c) whether it is also a fact that India is
even lagging far behind compared to South
Korea, China and other developing
countries due to decline in the standard and
quality of research-work; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the
details thereof?
Rural electrification targets in
Jharkhand
†*167. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a target of
electrification of only 250 villages in
Jharkhand has been fixed under the Rajiv
Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana
during the year 2006-07 whereas target of
40 thousand villages has been fixed for
whole country in this regard;
(b) the number of villages in Jharkhand
without electricity;
(c) whether the number is highest  in
comparison to the other States;
(d) if so, the reasons for fixing a low
target for Jharkhand; and
(e) the amount allocated to Jharkhand
for the electrification of villages during the
said period?
Benches of Supreme Court
*168. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE
be pleased to state:
(a) the details of recommendations made
by parliamentary committees for setting

53
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
up of Benches of Supreme Court in the
South and North-East, so far;
(b) the reasons for non implementation
of these recommendations; and
(c) the steps Government propose to
take to fulfill the aspirations of the people
in far flung regions?
Killing of a woman as Sati
*169. SHRIMATI SYEDA
ANWARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
 Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh
a 95 year old woman was killed after her
four sons pushed her on to her husband's
funeral pyre claiming it to be a "Sati" Ritual;
(b) if so, whether Government will take
it up seriously with the Government of
Madhya Pradesh as the Chief Minister
asserted that this incident could not be
prevented as the village was too remote for
anyone to act; and
(c) whether Government will issue
detailed guidelines to deal with such a
situation after taking State Governments
in confidence?
Change in CBSE curricula
*170. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact the CBSE has
added courses, changed the curricula and
have announced other changes frequently;
(b) whether CBSE consults experts
before making major changes;
(c) whether it is a fact that despite a
number of representations the CBSE has
not been able to modernise and make
efficient the issue of marks certificates and
other documents; and
(d) what external advice will be sought
by the CBSE to effect changes in its own
administrative role and duties?
Categories of persons treated as
disabled
*171. SHRI THANGA TAMIL
SELVAN: Will the Minister of SOCIAL
JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the categories of persons treated as
'disabled' for the purpose of education and
employment;
(b) whether the quota for the disabled
is being filled up regularly; and
(c) whether there is any proposal to
increase the percentage of quota for the
disabled in view of the increasing number
of people with various kinds of disabilities?
Pre and Post-matric scholarship for
OBCs
†*172. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) the reasons for not following the
norms of granting cent per cent amount of
scholarship to the students belonging to
OBC studying in pre-matric and post-
matric classes by the Central Government
as is being done in the case of SC and ST
students of same category despite
continuous requests being made by the
Government of Madhya Pradesh to the

54
Centre for extending same facilities of
economic assistance to the students
belonging to OBC; and
(b) by when this demand would be
fulfilled?
IMRB-SRI report on education for
children
*173. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether as per a nation-wide survey
that was carried out by IMRB-SRI of
school going children aged 6 to 13 years,
almost 6.94 per cent of children in this age
group are out of school and out of this
massive 68.26 per cent are those who never
went to school and about 31.71 per cent
are those who dropped out after one or
more years of school;
(b) if so, what are the other main points
mentioned in the survey report;
(c) whether Government have
considered the survey report; and
(d) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to meet the situation?
Care of orphaned boys and girls
*174. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Care Homes
and Orphanages keep children upto the age
of 18 only;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is a fact that by the time
the orphan boys and girls reach the age of
18 they do not complete education enough
to enable them to get employment due to
factors such as ban on under age
employment etc.; and
(d) if so, whether Government propose
to provide for retention of orphans for some
more years, if not, the reasons therefor?
Opening of anganwadi kendras
*175. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE THAKUR:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
for opening up new anganwadi kendras in
the country in order to create employment
avenues during the current fiscal year;
(b) if so, the details thereof with the
number of posts proposed to be created
from this scheme in the country
particularly in Himachal Pradesh;
(c) the number of anganwadi kendras
proposed to be opened up in Himachal
Pradesh;
(d) whether any funds have been
allocated to the State for completion of this
scheme;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) by when the target of opening up
anganwadi kendras in the State is likely to
be achieved?
Health care in pregnancy and
children
*176. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a paper presented by the
Centre for Social Research in a recent
workshop organized by UNICEF addresses
the grave problem of dismal health care that

55
women receive throughout pregnancy and
child birth often resulting in a high number
of pregnancy related deaths;
(b) whether India in 2000 registered
1,37,000 maternal deaths per year, highest
in world;
(c) whether the paper suggested that
"safe motherhood" as a concept should be
promoted by dual focus of attention—
women's empowerment and improved
healthcare access and delivery; and
(d) the steps Government propose to
take to reduce pregnancy related deaths in
India?
Food processing units in the country
*177. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Government and non-
Government units of food processing
industries in the country and in each State
of the North Eastern Region;
(b) the percentage of fruits processed
out of the fruits produced in the whole of
the country; and
(c) the programme of Government (both
Central and State level) to increase the
percentage of processed fruits significantly?
Review of Electricity Act, 2003
*178. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Electricity Act, 2003
passed by the erstwhile NDA Government
sought to trifurcate the functioning of State
Electricity Board (SEB) work into
Generation, Transmission and Distribution
as part of the reforms suggested by IMF
and World Bank in electricity generation
and supply in India;
(b) if so, whether Government are aware
about the disastrous experience in 13 States
where these reforms were implemented; and
(c) if so, by when Government are going
to review the Act as promised in NCMP?
Abandoned widows and women
*179. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
there are lakhs of widows and women
abandoned by their husbands in the country
who are in dire state;
(b) whether Government are aware that
in Rajasthan alone there are 15.89 lakh
widows and another 15000 women
abandoned by their husbands while only
2.12 lakh get pension from Government;
and
(c) if so, whether Government have
done any country-wide survey to assess
the number and condition of such women
and how Government propose to provide
them help to lead a dignified life?
Differential tariff for electricity
*180. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to divide the electricity
consumption in the country into peak and
off-peak hours, with electricity costing
cheaper during the off-peak hours; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the December 4, 2006/Agrahayana 13, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and
Renewable Energy; Power; Science and Technology;
Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs;
Women and Child Development)

263
Fund for development of ocean and
earth science
†1174. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that setting up of
human resource fund is being considered
for infrastructure and development of the
education for continuity and development
of ocean and earth science;
(b) if so, by when this fund is expected
to be set up; and
(c) the steps taken by Government so
far to run the coordinated research and
development work for the deep knowledge
about earth and ocean?
Assessment of global warming on
Indian climates
1175. SHRI RAHUL BAJAJ: Will the
Minister of EARTH SCIENCES  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether an assessment of likely
impact of global warming on Indian climate
has been made;
(b) if so, what are its major findings;
and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Maintenance of food products
†1176. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY:
SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether food products get rotten
and become useless in absence of their
maintenance; and
(b) if so, the details of the efforts being
made by Government to prevent the
same?

264
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Investment in food processing sector
†1177. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of investment likely to be
made on food processing sector during the
Eleventh Five Year Plan;
(b) whether there is a possibility for
setting up new food testing laboratories,
slaughter houses, cold storages and National
Meat Board in the Eleventh Five Year Plan;
and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Policy for development of food
processing industries in Sikkim
1178. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated a policy for development and
promotion of food processing industries in
Sikkim;
(b) if so, the details alongwith salient
features thereof; and
(c) by when the said policy is likely to
be implemented?
Assistance for setting up of food
processing and training centres
1179. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES  be pleased to state:
(a) whether assistance is being provided
by Government for setting up food
processing and training centres,
entrepreneurship development programme,
and creation of infrastructure and taking
up degree/diploma courses;
(b) if so, the details thereof for each
category; and
(c) the details of assistance provided
during the past three years in the country,
State-wise?
Food processing centres in the
country
1180. SHRI SUDARSHAN
AKARAPU: Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to set up 500 food processing centres in
different parts of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the number of centres set up State-
wise, as on 31st October, 2006; and
(d) the total amount sanctioned and
spent under the scheme?
Food safety and standard authority for
food processing sector
1181. SHRI C.
RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to set
up the food safety and standard authority
to oversee the entire food manufacturing
and processing sectors;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is being ensured to check
food adulteration;
(d) if not, the steps taken by

265
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Government to create standards and
guidelines on food;
(e) whether food imported into the
country is being monitored and approved
by the above authority before entry; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Establishment of economic zones
under Food Processing Industries
†1182. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the State-wise number of economic
zones established till date under his
Ministry; and
(b) if not, the reasons therefor?
Literacy in rural and urban areas
1183. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 26 per cent
of the households in rural areas and 8 per
cent in the urban areas, do not have a single
member in the age group of 15 years who
could read and write a simple message and
that 64 per cent of men and 45 per cent of
women are literate only; and
(b) if so, what are the targets fixed,
period-wise and percentage-wise under the
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan to increase the
literacy rate in the country as a whole in
rural and urban areas?
Accreditation of universities by NAAC
1184. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of parameters on which
the National Assessment and Accreditation
Council assesses the accreditation of a
university;
(b) the details of weightage assigned to
each of the parameters;
(c) the parameter-wise scores of the
universities accredited so far;
(d) whether it is a fact that the non-
academic parameters carry more weight as
compared to academic parameters; and
(e) if so, whether Government propose
to correct the weightage?
Fees of IIMs
1185. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that fees and
other charges for students in IIMs are very
high and beyond the reach of even students
belonging to middle class family;
(b) if so, what are the reasons for such
high fees in those institutions;
(c) whether it is also a fact that these
IIMs have again decided to increase the
fees from the academic year 2007 and if so,
the details thereof and the reasons therefor;
and

266
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(d) whether any subsidies is being given
to those institutions at present and if so,
the details thereof?
Operation of fake universities
†1186. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that many fake universities are
running in different parts of the country;
(b) the States where fake universities
were discovered by Government after the
cases of evaluation of answer sheets in
Meerut and fake university in Mathura
came into light;
(c) the measures taken by Government
to check them and the extent of success
achieved by Government in this matter;
(d) whether Government would take
any action in the direction of making local
administration accountable for fake
universities; and
(e) if not, how these fake universities
would completely be checked?
College of architecture at Guwahati
1187. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up a
college of architecture in Guwahati, Assam;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether such an institute is also
proposed to be set up in Orissa to bridge
the gap in higher educational facilities in
this State; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
IIIT in Orissa
1188. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Chief Minister of Orissa
has made a request to the Hon'ble Prime
Minister for establishment of an Indian
Institute of Information Technology (IIIT)
at Bhubaneswar in view of the vast growth
potential in IT sector;
(b) whether the State Government has
sent a detailed project in the matter to the
Centre; and
(c) if so, the status thereof and the time
frame within which the approval would be
accorded and conveyed to the State,
especially when no reputed institute like
NIS, IIT and IIM has been established in
the State?
Mandatory accreditation of
universities and colleges
1189. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government consider
making accreditation mandatory for
universities and colleges, if not, the reasons
therefor;

267
(b) whether Government would
consider linking annual grants to a
university with its accreditation score;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor;
(d) whether Government would also
consider giving functional and financial
autonomy to the universities with higher
accreditation score; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Job oriented education system
†1190.SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL:
DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to give weightage to a job oriented education
system having felt the need to bring about
changes in the present education system;
(b) if so, the kind of changes
Government are considering to bring about
in the present education system and the
roadmap thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Development and expansion of
research
†1191. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is
absolute need of development and
expansion in the field of research in the
country;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that in
comparison to China, America, Japan and
other European countries, the public
expenditure on research in the country is
very low;
(c) if so, the part of Gross Domestic
Product being spent in the above said
countries and quantum thereof; and
(d) whether Government have fixed a
target to increase the percentage of the said
expenditure; and
(e) if so, the target thereof and by when
this target would be achieved?
Moily Committee Report
1192. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE:
SHRI DARA SINGH:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether oversight (Moily)
Committee has submitted its report to
Government for implementation of
proposed 27 per cent OBC quota in Central
educational institutions;
(b) if so, what are the main
recommendations made by the Committee;
(c) whether Government has so far
examined contentious "issue of creamy
layer" as well recommendations for creation
of new infrastructure in Central educational
institutions in order to admit 54 per cent
more students from next year; and
(d) whether Government has agreed to
Committee's recommendations for revision
of financial package needed to implement
the quota-from Rs. 16,500 crore to
Rs. 17,200 crore?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

268
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Irregularities in textbooks of NCERT
1193. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the number of satellites of the planet Saturn
has been mentioned as over 30 in the eighth
standard science textbook (first edition in
January, 2004) and as about 18 in the
geography textbook (first edition in
February, 2006) of sixth standard of
NCERT;
(b) if so, the reasons for reduction in
number of satellites of Saturn between 2004
and 2006; and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to
publish correct facts regarding geography
and science in the textbooks being released
by NCERT which is the premier research
organization in the country for education?
Directives of Supreme Court on OBC
reservation
†1194. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Supreme Court had
issued any directives with regard to 27 per
cent reservations to OBC in institutes of
higher learning; if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether the court has passed any
directions with regard to reservation to those
persons of SC, ST and OBC who fall within
the creamy layer; if so, the action being
taken in this regard;
(c) whether women belonging to the
above said categories are being considered
for special quota in reservation; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Universities offering distance
education
†1195. SHRI JAI NARAIN PRASAD
NISHAD: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) the names of the Central
Universities, State universities, State open
universities, deemed universities and
institutes of national importance offering
courses of studies through correspondence/
distance education;
(b) the total number of students enrolled
in these universities and institutes at
present;
(c) the total number of students who
have passed from these universities and
institutions;
(d) the details of the boys/girls/SC/ST/
OBC and minority students studying in
these universities and institutions; and
(e) the total number of students who
have either secured employment or got
promotion in Central and State Government
offices on the basis of their educational
qualifications after obtaining education
through correspondence/distance learning?
Shortages of trained computer
professionals
1196. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the acute shortage of trained computer
professionals in the country against the
demands of a rapidly growing IT industry;
(b) if so, whether Government has a
proposal to open or facilitate opening
technical institutes focused on IT industry,

269
to train large number of people for
